description.value: A multimodal fMRI and RAC-PET study examined beer-flavor cue responses in male beer drinkers and their relationship to ventral-striatal dopamine release and motivation to drink.

spans.text: This multi-modal imaging study sheds new light on the relationships between drug cue-induced human limbic frontal activity and VST dopamine changes.

value: we hypothesized that beer flavor would: 1) induce activation in right VST, 2) activate medial and bilateral OFC primary reinforcer valuation sites (Plassmann et al., 2010, Kringelbach and Rolls, 2004), 3) produce PFC/OFC BOLD activation that correlated with right VST DA release (from PET), and 4) increase wanting and desire for beer.

description.value: A multimodal, within-subject, non-interventional study in healthy male beer drinkers; participants underwent fMRI and PET on separate days.

a priori ROIs were defined in all: 1) the same anatomical right VST ROI (A-P center at y=12) used in Oberlin et al., (2013) that showed a CS-elicited DA response to beer flavor; 2) left and right OFC (two 8 mm radius spheres, excluding white matter, centered on [±24, 30, −16]; Kringelbach and Rolls, 2004 , Kareken et al., 2013 ), identified by meta-analysis as sensitive to primary reinforcers; 3) medial OFC/ventromedial PFC (8 mm radius sphere centered on [0, 32, −20]), where responses are thought to reflect “goal value” ( Plassmann et al., 2010 , Plassmann et al., 2007 )—the imagined value of a reinforcer at the time of choice.
